solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Express perhaps support for book

parts.note: the Daily Express is a British newspaper, so it is an example of a paper
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: Someone champions a particular book while sounding urgent about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb, but the 'perhaps' shows it is an example: the Daily Express, a British national newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A paperback is a book bound in a soft card cover rather than hard boards.

clue.text: Spend a long time in corridor

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Someone waits for ages in a hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a narrow way connecting rooms, a synonym for a corridor.

clue.text: Father's taking motorway in vast plain

indicators.note: taking says the father's word holds the motorway letter within it

parts.note: papa is father, so father's gives PAPA plus S
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Dad drives a motorway across a huge flat plain.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grasslands of South America, especially Argentina.

clue.text: Really out of energy, in this court exchange

indicators.note: out of says the energy letter leaves the word really

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A tennis exchange on court is said to have truly drained someone's energy.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or squash, a rally is a long sequence of shots exchanged before a point ends.

clue.text: A brief point is relevant

parts.note: PT is the short form of point

explanation.surface: A short point is pertinent to the discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt describes something suitable or pertinent, a synonym for relevant.

clue.text: Upset entering dark early class

indicators.note: upset suggests the letters of the two words are knocked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A child is upset at going into a dark room for a morning lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindergarten is the nursery or first school class for very young children.

clue.text: Way in by means of long avenue

indicators.note: in says the street abbreviation sits inside the word for by means of

parts.note: via means by way of or by means of
ST is the abbreviation for street, a kind of way

explanation.surface: A route is described as reached by way of a long avenue.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a long narrow view, often seen down an avenue of trees or buildings.

clue.text: Struggle to swallow protein: townsman spoken of for non-meat option

indicators.note: to swallow says the word for struggle takes the egg inside it

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
an egg is a source of protein

indicators.note: spoken of says the townsman's word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a burgher is a citizen of a town

explanation.surface: A townsperson battles to eat a protein dish and goes for the vegetarian choice.
explanation.walkthrough: BURGHER and BURGER sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie burger is a vegetarian patty, an alternative to one made of beef.

clue.text: Second best and late, break off abruptly

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
the late means the dead

explanation.surface: A runner coming second best and late suddenly gives up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop dead is to halt suddenly, the idiom for ceasing all at once.

clue.text: Alien trapped in Alpine tunnel is a fool

indicators.note: trapped in says the alien is caught inside the tunnel's name

parts.note: the Simplon tunnel runs through the Alps between Switzerland and Italy
ET is the film alien, the extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An extra-terrestrial stuck inside a mountain tunnel is mocked as foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The Simplon is a famous railway tunnel under the Alps; ET goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a person lacking in sense or intelligence, so a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Paint, a gallon a write-off

parts.note: a write-off is something counted as a total loss

explanation.surface: A can of paint is wasted, a whole gallon written off.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a type of paint that dries to a shiny finish.

clue.text: Whatever happens, never mind the price

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in any case, regardless of circumstances
second meaning, read literally: at whatever rate of charge

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes the phrase literally, a rate being a price; the blogger calls it double-ish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in any event, and taken word by word it means whatever the charge.

clue.text: In friendly spirit, claim bay for redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment means rebuilding, so the letters of the two words are reshaped

explanation.surface: A developer politely stakes a claim to a bay for building.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicably means in a friendly, good-natured way, without quarrelling.

clue.text: For a Spaniard, the regular team

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
even means regular or uniform

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is said to have a settled, regular side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a Spaniard, the' asks for the Spanish word for 'the', EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has eleven players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Starting to get light, after removing front shade

indicators.note: after removing front says the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: dawning means the day starting to get light

explanation.surface: Early morning comes and someone takes down the shade at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas sheet stretched over a window or shopfront for shelter from sun.

clue.text: A little change in weather: wind

indicators.note: a little change says the letters of the word are slightly rearranged

explanation.surface: A forecaster mentions a slight shift in the weather, with some wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' tempts as a weather word, but it is the verb, rhyming with find.
explanation.definitionFit: To wreathe is to coil or twine around something, as a vine winds about a post.

clue.text: Temporary accommodation at American college grounds

parts.note: a camp is a set of tents or huts for temporary lodging
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Short-term housing is set up on an American college site.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the land and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Accept responsibility of arranging funeral?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to take on a task
second meaning, playful: the work of an ..., who arranges funerals

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: the verb is treated as what an undertaker does. The blogger puts it between a double definition and a cryptic hint.
explanation.definitionFit: To undertake a job is to commit to it; an undertaker is a funeral director.

clue.text: Part of treasure trove is consciously old-fashioned

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hoard of buried treasure is described as deliberately antique in style.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro style deliberately imitates fashions of the past, so it is knowingly dated.

clue.text: Mile added into a little circuit

indicators.note: added into says the mile's letter goes inside the phrase for a little

parts.note: a bit means a little

explanation.surface: A short running circuit is lengthened by a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is the bounds or circuit of a place, its compass or scope.

clue.text: Prepares to pour tea? Is being ruined

definitions.meaning: first meaning, playful: tea is poured once it goes into the teapot
second meaning: deteriorates, falls into ruin

explanation.walkthrough: Despite the look of 'pour tea', there is no anagram here: the first half is a whimsical literal reading of the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to decline badly, while literally the tea leaves head into the teapot.

clue.text: Little amphibian featured in English newspaper

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A small newt appears in a British newspaper story.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small amphibian; the word is mostly crossword-only.

clue.text: Composer's hard day, struggling by noon

definitions.note: the definition includes the 's because the clue reads 'the composer is hard day struggling by noon'; the 's is the link verb, so the noun phrase still names the person

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: struggling suggests the day's letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A composer has a tough day, battling until midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian classical composer of over a hundred symphonies.

clue.text: Amazingly true: roses turned up!

definitions.note: past participle used adjectivally, matching the answer

indicators.note: amazingly suggests the letters of the two words are rearranged in a surprising way

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise that roses have actually appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' seems to mean arrived, but it is the definition: tilted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose that tilts upward at the tip, a borrowing from French.
